name: Collagen
description: The most abundant structural protein in mammals, providing tensile strength and structural support to connective tissue.
applications: Tissue engineering scaffolds, wound dressings, skin substitutes, bone grafts

name: Chitosan
description: A biodegradable, biocompatible polysaccharide derived from chitin with antimicrobial properties.
applications: Wound healing, drug delivery, hemostatic agents, tissue scaffolds

name: Cellulose
description: A structural polysaccharide made of glucose units, widely used in nanocellulose and bacterial cellulose forms.
applications: Wound dressings, drug delivery matrices, scaffolds, packaging

name: Alginate
description: A biocompatible, gel-forming polysaccharide that crosslinks in the presence of divalent cations like calcium.
applications: Cell encapsulation, wound dressings, hydrogel scaffolds, drug delivery

name: Gelatin
description: A water-soluble protein derived from partial hydrolysis of collagen, commonly used in hydrogel formulations.
applications: Hydrogels, drug delivery capsules, tissue scaffolds, bioprinting bioinks

name: Silk Fibroin
description: A natural fibrous protein known for high tensile strength, biocompatibility, and controllable degradation.
applications: Sutures, tissue scaffolds, drug delivery, bone and cartilage regeneration

name: PLGA
source: Synthetic (lactic acid and glycolic acid copolymer)
description: A biodegradable, FDA-approved copolymer whose degradation rate can be tuned by adjusting the lactide-to-glycolide ratio.
applications: Drug delivery microspheres, sutures, tissue engineering scaffolds

name: PLA
description: A biodegradable thermoplastic polyester derived from renewable resources, commonly used in 3D-printed scaffolds.
applications: Orthopedic implants, sutures, 3D-printed scaffolds, drug delivery

name: Hydroxyapatite
description: A naturally occurring mineral form of calcium apatite that closely resembles the mineral component of bone.
applications: Bone grafts, dental implants, bone cement, coating for orthopedic implants

name: Bioactive Glass
description: A biocompatible glass that bonds to bone tissue by forming a hydroxyapatite layer upon contact with body fluids.
applications: Bone regeneration, dental applications, wound healing, scaffold coatings

name: Titanium
source: Synthetic (refined ore, often as Ti-6Al-4V alloy)
description: A lightweight, corrosion-resistant metal with excellent biocompatibility and mechanical strength.
applications: Orthopedic implants, dental implants, joint replacements, bone plates

name: PEG
description: Polyethylene glycol is a hydrophilic, non-immunogenic polymer widely used to form hydrogels and modify drug pharmacokinetics.
applications: Hydrogel scaffolds, drug delivery, PEGylation of proteins, cell encapsulation

name: PCL
description: Polycaprolactone is a slow-degrading, biocompatible polyester with good mechanical properties for long-term scaffolds.
applications: Long-term tissue scaffolds, drug delivery, sutures, 3D-printed constructs

name: Hyaluronic Acid
description: A naturally occurring glycosaminoglycan found in connective tissue, known for high water retention and viscoelasticity.
applications: Dermal fillers, viscosupplementation, wound healing, hydrogel scaffolds

name: Fibrin
description: A natural protein formed during blood clotting, used as a biological glue and cell delivery matrix.
applications: Surgical sealants, cell delivery scaffolds, wound healing, tissue regeneration

name: Elastin
description: A highly elastic structural protein that provides resilience and stretch recovery to tissues like blood vessels and skin.
applications: Vascular grafts, skin regeneration, elastic tissue scaffolds

name: Keratin
description: A fibrous structural protein known for mechanical durability and self-assembly properties in regenerated form.
applications: Wound dressings, nerve regeneration, drug delivery, hemostatic materials

name: Dextran
description: A branched polysaccharide composed of glucose units, widely used as a hydrogel and drug carrier backbone.
applications: Drug delivery, hydrogels, plasma volume expanders, bioprinting

name: Agarose
description: A gel-forming polysaccharide purified from agar, valued for thermoreversible gelation and biocompatibility.
applications: Cell culture scaffolds, electrophoresis gels, tissue engineering matrices

name: Calcium Phosphate
description: A family of biocompatible mineral compounds structurally similar to the inorganic phase of bone.
applications: Bone cement, bone graft substitutes, dental fillers, coatings for implants
